letter:
Dear Cardiologist,

Re: Bernard Halloran, 71

Bernard was found to be in atrial fibrillation at a routine check 18 months ago. He has stayed in rate-controlled AF on bisoprolol 2.5 mg, resting rate 70 to 80, and takes apixaban 5 mg bd without bleeding. He has no chest pain, breathlessness or dizziness and still plays lawn bowls twice a week. Echo last year: normal LV function, mild left atrial dilatation. He would like a specialist opinion on whether rhythm control is worth considering long term.

Kind regards,
Dr Fiona Lattimore
note: Stable, asymptomatic rate-controlled AF with normal LV function asking for a long-term opinion is routine.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Marjorie Pell, 68

Marjorie has right hip osteoarthritis, confirmed on X-ray with marked joint space loss. Over the past year her pain has become constant, she wakes most nights, and she can now only walk about 200 metres with a stick. Twelve months of physiotherapy, weight loss of 6 kg, paracetamol and intermittent celecoxib have not helped enough. She is otherwise well, BMI 29, and keen to discuss hip replacement.

Regards,
Dr Owen Castellano
note: Painful, disabling hip osteoarthritis that failed conservative care is semi-urgent: significant dysfunction but chronic and degenerative.

letter:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Kirsty Abernethy, 34

Kirsty has had episodic migraine without aura since her teens. Attacks occur about three times a month and respond to sumatriptan within two hours. Neurological examination is normal and there has been no change in the character of her headaches. She is not keen on taking a daily preventer while she is trying to conceive next year and would value advice on safe options and on the role of newer treatments.

Kind regards,
Dr Harriet Boyce
note: Long-standing, unchanged, well-controlled migraine with a normal exam and an advice question is routine.

letter:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Dimitri Vlahos, 46

Dimitri was diagnosed with pulmonary sarcoidosis in Adelaide in 2021 and treated with prednisolone for a year. He has been off treatment for two years with no symptoms. Recent spirometry and gas transfer are normal and his chest X-ray shows only small residual hilar nodes, unchanged since 2023. He has moved to the area for work and needs ongoing specialist follow-up. Previous letters enclosed.

Regards,
Dr Petra Lindqvist

history.note: No previous outpatient referrals at this service.

note: Quiescent sarcoidosis with normal lung function being transferred for follow-up is routine.

letter:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Colin Ashworth, 63

Colin has had heartburn for many years, managed with pantoprazole 40 mg. He asked me to refer him because the heartburn is no longer fully controlled and he would like to discuss long-term PPI use. On questioning he also mentions that over the last two months food has started sticking behind his breastbone, first with steak and now with bread, and it is getting steadily worse. Weight is stable. He is an ex-smoker and drinks about 20 standard drinks a week. Bloods are normal.

Kind regards,
Dr Rhonda Kilpatrick
note: Progressive difficulty swallowing is a gastroenterology red flag, so this is urgent despite the routine reflux framing.

letter:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Yvette Marchetti, 52

Yvette has had facial rosacea for about five years with flushing and papules. Topical ivermectin helped initially but she has relapsed and would like to discuss oral treatment or vascular laser. While examining her I also looked at a mole on her upper back that her husband says has darkened and spread over the last few months. It is 9 mm, asymmetric, with two shades of brown, a black area and an irregular border. She has fair skin and a history of sunburn. She is otherwise well.

Regards,
Dr Gerald Nkemelu
note: A changing, asymmetric, irregular pigmented lesion is suspected melanoma, so the dermatology referral is urgent; one dermatology entry covers both skin issues.

letter:
Dear Cardiologist,

Re: Raymond Oduya, 58

Raymond describes occasional skipped beats for the past year, mostly in the evening after coffee. A Holter in 2024 showed frequent ventricular ectopics. He is a retired electrician, non-smoker, on perindopril for blood pressure. Last week, while carrying shopping up the stairs to his flat, he blacked out for a few seconds and woke on the landing; his wife saw no jerking. He felt fine afterwards. ECG today: sinus rhythm, left ventricular hypertrophy. He would like reassurance about the palpitations.

Kind regards,
Dr Simone Achterberg
note: Syncope on exertion is a cardiology red flag, so this is urgent even though the letter is framed around benign palpitations.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Lucas Ferreira, 39

Lucas felt a sudden snap in his left heel while pushing off at indoor cricket five days ago, as if someone had kicked him. He has been walking flat-footed since. There is a palpable gap 4 cm above the calcaneal insertion and Thompson's test is positive. Ultrasound yesterday confirmed a complete Achilles tendon rupture with a 12 mm gap. I have placed him in a boot in equinus. He is a fit non-smoker and a site manager.

Regards,
Dr Anika Rasmussen
note: A complete Achilles rupture five days old needs a time-critical decision on surgery, so it is urgent.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Tayla Brooker, 24

Tayla twisted her right knee landing awkwardly at netball eight days ago. Since then she cannot fully straighten it; it sticks at about 20 degrees short of full extension and she is on crutches. There is a moderate effusion and medial joint line tenderness. MRI this week shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus flipped into the notch, with an intact ACL. She is a primary school teacher and otherwise well.

Kind regards,
Dr Mitchell Varga
note: A locked knee from a displaced bucket-handle meniscal tear is a time-critical orthopaedic problem, so it is urgent.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Graham Tulloch, 61

Graham ruptured his right Achilles tendon playing squash three years ago. It was treated in a boot without surgery and healed well. He now walks without limitation and plays golf, but notices his right calf is a little weaker when climbing steep hills and cannot quite do a full single-leg heel raise. There is no pain. A friend had a tendon reconstruction and Graham would like to know whether surgery might help him.

Regards,
Dr Leonie Faraday

history.note: 2023: Right Achilles rupture managed non-operatively in fracture clinic, discharged to GP.

note: An old healed Achilles rupture with minimal dysfunction is a chronic problem; considering surgery does not make it urgent, so it is routine.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Edna Polglase, 74

I referred Edna in August for her left knee osteoarthritis and she asked me to write again as she has not yet received an appointment. Her symptoms are unchanged: aching after walking more than a kilometre and some stiffness in the mornings. She manages well with paracetamol and a hydrotherapy class. X-ray shows moderate medial compartment narrowing. She would like to discuss options when she is seen.

Kind regards,
Dr Brendan Whitcombe

history.note: August 2026: Referred to orthopaedics for left knee osteoarthritis, triaged routine.

note: A chaser letter for the same unchanged knee osteoarthritis already on the routine list; no new entry and no change.

letter:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Callum Nguyen, 31

Callum has recently joined our practice. He has left-sided ulcerative colitis diagnosed in 2023 and has had three mild flares this year, each settling with a mesalazine enema course within two weeks. Between flares he has normal bowel habit. Calprotectin was 310 during the last flare and 80 afterwards. He has not had steroids. He would like to discuss maintenance options to reduce the flares.

Regards,
Dr Juliette Ambrose

waitlist.problem: ulcerative colitis with recurrent mild flares
iron deficiency anaemia with weight loss

history.note: June 2026: Referred by previous GP for ulcerative colitis with recurrent mild flares, triaged semi-urgent.

note: The new GP is re-referring the same colitis already listed at the right category; no second entry.

letter:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Priya Raghunathan, 45

Further to my referral last week regarding the pigmented lesion on Priya's left calf, I am sending the dermoscopy findings from our skin check. The lesion measures 8 mm with asymmetry, an atypical pigment network and regression structures. Clinically it is unchanged since my first letter. I remain concerned about melanoma and have not biopsied it, pending your review. She has no palpable nodes.

Kind regards,
Dr Toby Hargreaves

history.note: Last week: Referred to dermatology for suspected melanoma of the left calf, triaged urgent.

note: Supporting information for a suspected melanoma already listed as urgent; the entry should stay as it is with no duplicate.

letter:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Norman Fitzsimmons, 66

I referred Norman in May with looser stools and bloating, which we thought might be irritable bowel. Things have changed. He now opens his bowels four to five times a day, the stools are loose and occasionally dark, and he has lost 7 kg over three months without trying. Hb 121 (was 140 in May), ferritin 14. He has never had a colonoscopy and did not return his bowel screening kit.

Regards,
Dr Cheryl Odhiambo

history.note: May 2026: Referred to gastroenterology for altered bowel habit and bloating, triaged routine.

note: Unexplained weight loss with bowel change is a red flag; the existing routine entry should be updated to urgent, not duplicated.

letter:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Stavros Kallis, 59

I referred Stavros in July with tingling and clumsiness in both hands, which I thought might be carpal tunnel syndrome. Over the past two months he has developed weakness: he struggles with buttons and keys and has dropped tools at work. I can now see wasting of the first dorsal interosseous muscles on both sides and fasciculations in both forearms and the left calf. Reflexes are brisk. Nerve conduction studies are booked but not yet done.

Kind regards,
Dr Imogen Pascoe

history.note: July 2026: Referred to neurology for bilateral hand tingling and clumsiness, ?carpal tunnel, triaged routine.

note: Progressive weakness with wasting and fasciculations suggests motor neurone disease; the existing routine neurology entry should be raised to urgent.

letter:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Lorraine Duggan, 64

You have Lorraine on your list for her chronic cough. She is a current smoker of 40 pack-years. In the past fortnight she has coughed up streaks of blood on three occasions and has lost her appetite. A chest X-ray this week shows a new 3 cm opacity in the right upper lobe that was not present on her film two years ago. CT has been requested. She is otherwise managing at home.

Regards,
Dr Vikram Seth

history.note: April 2026: Referred to respiratory for chronic cough in a smoker, triaged semi-urgent.

note: Haemoptysis in a smoker with a new mass suggests lung cancer; the semi-urgent entry should be updated to urgent.

letter:
Dear Cardiologist,

Re: Wendy Lockhart, 69

I referred Wendy last month with new chest tightness on exertion. Since starting aspirin, atorvastatin and a GTN spray she has had only one episode, walking quickly uphill, which settled with rest. She feels much better and is keen to travel to Queensland for a month. Given her improvement, would it be possible to change her appointment to a routine one so she can go away?

Kind regards,
Dr Patrick Moloney

history.note: October 2026: Referred to cardiology for new exertional chest pain, triaged urgent.

note: The guideline forbids lowering urgency on a letter alone; the urgent entry stays and the request is flagged for review.

letter:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Hamish Carrigan, 57

Hamish is on your urgent list after a positive bowel screening test. He was very anxious about colonoscopy and bought a pharmacy faecal occult blood kit, which came back negative last week. He has no bowel symptoms, no weight loss and normal bloods. In view of the negative repeat test, I am happy for his appointment to be downgraded to routine if you agree.

Regards,
Dr Naomi Szabo

history.note: September 2026: Referred to gastroenterology after a positive bowel screening test, triaged urgent.

note: A letter alone cannot lower an urgent entry; it stays urgent and the downgrade request is flagged for review.

letter:
Dear Cardiologist,

Re: Douglas Ventura, 55

Thank you for seeing Douglas, who I have been worried about. I arranged an echocardiogram and an exercise stress test last month and the results are attached. I would be grateful for your opinion and management. He is a non-smoker and takes no regular medication. Please let me know if you need anything further.

Kind regards,
Dr Lisette Morrow
note: No symptoms are described and the echo and stress test results said to be attached are missing, so the GP must be asked before booking.

letter:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Agnes Forsythe, 77

Agnes came in today asking to see a skin specialist about a spot that is bothering her. I would be grateful if you could review it and advise on management. She has hypertension and type 2 diabetes, on metformin and amlodipine, and lives independently. Her daughter will bring her to the appointment.

Regards,
Dr Ethan Mulvaney
note: The lesion is not described at all (site, size, change, appearance), so the category cannot be set and the GP must be asked.

letter:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Selina Okafor, 42

Selina had an MRI brain last week, which shows some changes. The report is attached for your review. I would appreciate your assessment and advice regarding further investigation and management. She has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker.

Kind regards,
Dr Rupert Galloway
note: Neither the reason for the MRI nor the findings are given and the report is not attached, so the GP must be asked before booking.

letter:
Dear ENT Surgeon,

Re: Jasmine Tran, 23

Jasmine has had seven episodes of acute tonsillitis in the past twelve months, each needing antibiotics and two to three days off university. Two episodes were confirmed streptococcal on swab. She had a peritonsillar abscess drained in ED in March. Between episodes she is well. She would like to discuss tonsillectomy.

Kind regards,
Dr Malcolm Adeyemi
note: ENT is not a service this clinic runs, so nothing is booked and the referral is flagged for redirection.

letter:
Dear Ophthalmologist,

Re: Clive Bannister, 78

Clive has noticed gradually worsening blurred vision in both eyes over two years, with glare from oncoming headlights making night driving difficult. His optometrist found bilateral cataracts, worse on the right, with best corrected acuity 6/18 right and 6/12 left. He has no eye pain or redness. He would like to be considered for cataract surgery so he can keep driving.

Regards,
Dr Beatrice Yuen

history.note: March 2026: Referred to dermatology for actinic keratoses on the scalp, triaged routine.

note: Ophthalmology is not run here, so it is flagged and nothing new is booked; the patient's unrelated dermatology entry stays unchanged.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Terrence Mahoney, 64

Terrence's PSA has risen from 3.1 last year to 6.8 on two readings a month apart. Free-to-total ratio is 0.11. Digital rectal exam shows a firm, mildly enlarged prostate without a discrete nodule. He has mild nocturia but no haematuria or bone pain. His brother was diagnosed with prostate cancer at 60. I would be grateful for assessment and consideration of MRI and biopsy.

Kind regards,
Dr Sunita Iyer
note: A rising PSA needs urology, which this service does not run; nothing is booked and it is flagged for redirection.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Keith Brannigan, 62

I would be grateful for two opinions. First, over the past three weeks Keith has developed tightness across his chest when walking up the hill to the station, easing within minutes of stopping. He has hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia and is an ex-smoker. ECG today shows no acute changes. Second, he has had mild aching in his left knee for several years. X-ray shows mild osteoarthritis; he walks 5 km daily and manages with occasional paracetamol, but would like advice on keeping active.

Kind regards,
Dr Rosalind Achebe
note: New exertional chest pain is urgent cardiology; mild, well-managed knee osteoarthritis is routine orthopaedics; both get booked.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Rosemary Kettering, 70

Rosemary has several raised, waxy brown lesions on her back and chest that have been present for years. They look typical of seborrhoeic keratoses and are not changing, but they catch on her clothing and she would like advice on removal. Separately, she has noticed gradual hearing loss in both ears over three years and struggles in noisy restaurants. Her audiogram shows bilateral high-frequency sensorineural loss and she would like an ENT opinion about hearing aids.

Regards,
Dr Anton Petrakis

waitlist.problem: suspected squamous cell carcinoma in transplant patient

note: Stable seborrhoeic keratoses are routine dermatology; the hearing loss needs ENT, which is not run, so that part is flagged.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Zachary Mbeki, 36

Zachary had a generalised tonic-clonic seizure at home on Saturday, witnessed by his partner, lasting about two minutes with confusion afterwards. He has never had one before. CT brain in ED was normal and he was discharged to see me. He has stopped driving. He also has type 1 diabetes and is overdue for his diabetic eye review, and I would appreciate a referral to ophthalmology for retinal screening.

Kind regards,
Dr Clarissa Vandenberg
note: A first seizure is urgent neurology; diabetic eye screening needs ophthalmology, which is not run here, so it is flagged.

letter:
Dear Cardiologist,

Re: Tamsin Holloway, 29

URGENT please. Tamsin is very anxious about palpitations, which she notices as a thud or skipped beat while lying in bed, a few times a week for six months. There is no dizziness, chest pain, breathlessness or fainting, and she runs three times a week without trouble. A 24-hour Holter showed occasional isolated ventricular ectopics only, and her echo is normal. Thyroid function and electrolytes are normal. She is very keen to be seen as soon as possible.

Kind regards,
Dr Fergus Delaney
note: Benign ectopics with a normal echo and no red flags are routine, whatever urgency the GP asks for.

letter:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Ingrid Solberg, 48

No rush with this one, a routine appointment is fine. Ingrid has a mole on her right thigh which she first noticed in winter. Over the past two months it has grown from about 5 mm to 10 mm, become darker with a blue-black area, and the border is now irregular. It bled once after rubbing on her jeans. She has fair skin and many moles. I suspect it is probably nothing but would value your opinion.

Regards,
Dr Harold Chikwanha
note: A rapidly growing, darkening, irregular pigmented lesion is suspected melanoma and urgent, whatever the GP says.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Barry Kowalski, 66

Please see urgently. Barry has left knee osteoarthritis that has worsened over two years. He now has daily pain, wakes at night, and can walk about 300 metres before he has to stop. He has had physiotherapy, weight loss and a steroid injection with only brief relief. X-ray shows bone-on-bone medial compartment narrowing. He is keen to have a knee replacement before his grandson's wedding next year.

Kind regards,
Dr Louisa Tan
note: Painful, disabling chronic knee osteoarthritis is semi-urgent; the request for urgent and the plan for surgery do not make it urgent.
